title: All journeys with actor, outcome, and session count
description: Returns all journeys with their actor, purpose, outcome, and the number of sessions in each.

title: Full event sequence for a journey
description: Returns the time-ordered sequence of events in a specific journey with event types and timestamps.

title: All objections grouped by category with resolution status
description: Returns all objection events with their category, whether they were resolved, and how.

title: All decision points with options considered and selected
description: Returns decision point events showing what was considered, chosen, and rejected.

title: Budget signals across journeys
description: Returns all budget signals with stated amounts, constraint types, and journey context.

title: Recommendation acceptance rate
description: Returns all recommendations with whether they were accepted, the product recommended, and the reason given.

title: User priority signals with dimensions and strength
description: Returns all priority signals showing what dimensions users care about most.

title: Conversion funnel event counts by type
description: Counts events of each interaction type across all journeys to show the funnel shape.
query:
PREFIX ix: <http://trustgraph.ai/ontology/interaction#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?eventType (COUNT(?event) AS ?count)
WHERE {
  ?event a ?eventType .
  ?eventType rdfs:subClassOf ix:InteractionEvent .
}
GROUP BY ?eventType
ORDER BY DESC(?count)

title: Objection resolution rate by category
description: Shows how often each objection type gets resolved vs stays unresolved.

title: Total spend per journey with product breakdown
description: Returns the products purchased and total spend for each completed journey.

title: Journey trigger events and types
description: Returns what triggered each journey — problem, occasion, deal, curiosity, or recommendation.

title: Events with both interaction and signal types (mixin pattern)
description: Finds events that carry both an interaction type and a signal type, demonstrating the mixin pattern.
